To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
experimental litter reduction in young females affects the development of the progeny’s brain and endocrine glands.

experimental reduction of litter size by removal of one of the uterine tubes of female rats at the age of 4. 5–5 or 8–9 months leads to changes in brain development and the activity of the adrenal cortex of their progeny.

experimental litter reduction in rats by removal of one tube of uterine horns at the age of 4.50–5.0 and 8.0–9.0 months led to a decrease in brain and endocrine organ weight, morphometric characteristics of the cortex, and the number of neurons, and to an increase in 3β-hodrosteroid dehydrogenaze activity in adrenal cortex in the progeny.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the number of fetuses on parameters of brain development and the endocrine glands of the progeny of young and old females.
the effect of experimental reduction of the number of offspring on parameters of brain development and the status of endocrine glands in rats.
the effect of the mother’s age and the number of pups in the litter on the brain development, behavior, and endocrine status of the progeny.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the progeny of young females with experimentally decreased litter size differed from the progenies of young females with intact litters and the progeny of old females with experimentallly reduced litters by parameters of brain development (brain weight, morphometric parameters of the cerebral cortex and its neurons), elevated plusmaze behavior and adrenal cortex function (activity of 3βHSD).

the progeny from young females with experimentally restricted litter size had a higher level of neuroendocrine stress, which was manifested in changes in the parameters of brain development and behavior.

the effect of litter reduction on the progeny is dependent on the age of the females and that the age of the mother is an important parameter in the study of the effect of the number of progeny on the progeny.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the progeny of females with experimentally decreased litter size at the age of 4.50.5 and 8.90 months had changes in the parameters of brain development and the endocrine status of the body.

, in rats, the age of the female at the time of pregnancy and litter reduction is one of the important factors determining the effects of litter reduction on brain and endocrine development of the progeny.
the effects of the early life environment on the development of brain and endocrinal glands are not the same for the progeny of young and old mothers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the progeny from young females, litter reduction by one uterine horn leads to the development of a number of changes in brain and endocrine system development.
litter reduction in females at the age of 4.50.5 and 8.09 months leads to a different effect in the development of brain and endocrinal glands in their progeny.
the age of the dam is a factor that can influence the effect of the number of fetuses on the development of the offspring.
